article_content: The US government has released an intelligence assessment alleging Syria's regime conducted a chemical weapons strike in suburban Damascus on August 21, 2013. According to the document, 1,429 people perished in the attack, including 426 children. Medical facilities reported treating 3,600 patients displaying sarin nerve agent symptoms within three hours, supported by 100+ videos showing victims' physical reactions. Satellite data and intercepted communications reportedly show Syrian chemical weapons units operating in 'Adra from August 18-21, near a known sarin production facility. Officials state rocket launches from regime-controlled territory occurred 90 minutes before initial reports. An intercepted message allegedly features a senior Syrian official confirming chemical weapons use and expressing concern about UN investigators. Analysts conclude rebel forces lacked both chemical weapons capabilities and technical capacity to stage such an incident. The report suggests the regime escalated to chemical warfare after failing to dislodge opposition fighters from Damascus suburbs using conventional tactics. While citing multiple evidence streams, the document notes some intelligence remains classified to protect sources.

Satellietdata en gekapte kommunikasie dui daarop dat Sirië se chemiese wapenpersoneel van 18 tot 21 Augustus in 'Adra naby 'n sarien-produksie-area gewerk het. Amptenare meld vuurpyl-lanserings vanaf regeringsbeheerde gebiede het 90 minute voor die eerste aanvalberigte plaasgevind. article_content: A Suffolk teenager is set to make history this weekend by becoming Britain's youngest pub licensee upon turning 18. Charlie Watts, currently 17, will assume leadership of The Cherry Tree in Yaxley - a family establishment operated by his parents for 11 years. Initially seeking part-time work after school, Charlie's parents surprised him by entrusting full management responsibilities. The transition coincides with father Andy's new career move, creating an opportunity for the family business succession. Having assisted at the pub since age seven, Charlie reflects: 'Growing up here gave me unexpected training - interacting with patrons taught me more than I realized.' Mother Nikki notes her son's growing professionalism while acknowledging the challenges of late-night operations. The Watts family joins other notable young hospitality pioneers, including 12-year-old Chris Hardacre who legally served alcohol in 2006 through a legislative loophole.

Charlie, wat van sy sewejarige ouderdom af by die kroeg gehelp het, deel: 'Om hier groot te word het my onbewustelik voorberei - deur met klante te gesels het ek meer geleer as wat ek besef het.' Ma Nikki sien haar seun se toenemende professionalisme, maar erken die uitdagings van laatnagwerk. article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) – The Open Skies agreement has been finalized, enabling unrestricted transatlantic flights between European and U.S. cities starting March 2008. Airlines are now preparing for intensified competition, particularly targeting business travelers with expanded route options and premium services. British Airways confirmed plans to launch transatlantic flights from Paris, Frankfurt, Brussels, and Milan, featuring premium cabins but not exclusive business class. Virgin Atlantic is developing business-only flights from multiple European cities by 2009, currently negotiating orders for 10-15 aircraft. Heathrow's near-maximum capacity may limit new routes despite demand, prompting carriers like Maxjet to focus on Stansted. Silverjet CEO Lawrence Hunt criticized Heathrow's 'zoo-like' conditions but confirmed ongoing discussions about potential operations. Industry experts predict minimal business class price reductions but emphasize service innovation. Anthony Concil from IATA highlighted the agreement as a catalyst for market liberalization, stating: 'We've created a new playing field for carrier creativity.'

article_content: A Russian Soyuz spacecraft completed a precision landing in Kazakhstan's steppes on March 16, 2013, safely returning three astronauts from the International Space Station after weather-related delays. NASA's Kevin Ford alongside Russian cosmonauts Oleg Novitskiy and Evgeny Tarelkin touched down at 7:06 AM Moscow time following their 144-day Expedition 34 mission spanning 61 million miles (98 million km). The capsule landed upright despite heavy fog, with recovery teams confirming crew members were in good health. Footage showed astronauts wrapped in thermal blankets being transported to inflatable medical tents. This mission marked a historic leadership transition as Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield became only the second non-American/Russian commander in the ISS's 12-year operational history.

NASA se Kevin Ford saam met Russiese kosmonoute Oleg Novitskiy en Evgeny Tarelkin het 07:06 Moskou-tyd geland ná hul 144-dae Expeditie 34-missie van 98 miljoen kilometer. Die kapsel het regop geland ondanks dik mis, met reddingspanne wat die bemanning se goeie gesondheid bevestig het. Opnames het getoon hoe ruimtevaarders in termiese komberse na opblaasbare mediese tente geneem is. Dié missie het 'n historiese wissel van bevelvoering gesien toe Chris Hadfield, die eerste Kanadese, slegs die tweede nie-Amerikaanse/Russiese bevelvoerder in die ISS se 12-jaargeskiedenis geword het.

article_content: Eleven middle school students and their driver sustained injuries when their school bus veered off the road and collided with trees in Anaheim, California, on Thursday afternoon. Three individuals—the driver and two students—were hospitalized in critical condition following the 3:30 pm incident, according to Anaheim police spokesperson Lt. Bob Dunn. Nine other students received minor injuries, with most released to parental custody. Local broadcasts showed the Orange Unified School District bus tilted against a tree near Anaheim Hills Golf Course. Emergency crews required 20 minutes to extricate the trapped driver. The bus was transporting students from an El Rancho Charter Middle School extracurricular activity when the accident occurred, stated district superintendent Michael L. Christensen. Fourteen-year-old Jak Pintches described the bus losing control during a turn, striking a tree and lamp post. 'I was thrown across the aisle and injured my back,' he told the Orange County Register. A tree branch penetrated the vehicle, injuring another student's leg. Witnesses reported gasoline leaks prompted evacuation orders. Bystander Andrea Shurtz observed the bus 'flying down the hill' before impact, describing chaotic scenes of injured students calling for help. While the bus contained seat belts, authorities confirmed uncertainty about usage compliance. The driver, employed since 2010, had his safety record defended by family members. California Highway Patrol leads the ongoing investigation into the single-vehicle incident.

article_content: The historic Battle of Agincourt's 'arrow storm' will be recreated for the first time in six centuries. A collaborative Anglo-French initiative plans to assemble 1,000 archers to commemorate Henry V's pivotal 1415 victory. On October 25, 1415 – also a Friday – England's outnumbered forces triumphed near Azincourt (modern French spelling). The Agincourt Alliance, supported by historians and tourism groups, aims to stage a 'Big Shoot' using rubber-blunted arrows with wooden shafts and white feathers. Each participant will fire 30 arrows to recreate the historic volley. Historians hope this event will shed new light on debates about the longbow's decisive role. Contemporary estimates suggest 12,000-36,000 French troops faced 6,000-9,000 English, with the latter's longbows (effective to 250 yards) proving decisive. The muddy, sloping terrain hindered French knights' mobility, resulting in approximately 6,000 French casualties versus 400 English. While Shakespeare immortalized the victory, some scholars question whether tactical advantages rather than archery alone secured the win. The commemorative event will occur on the preserved battlefield, coinciding with other European war anniversaries. Strict safety protocols will govern the reenactment, prohibiting live weapons.

'n Gesamentlike Anglo-Franse inisiatief beplan om 1,000 boogskutters te versamel om Henry V se deurslaggewende 1415-oorwinning te herdenk. Op 25 Oktober 1415 – ook 'n Vrydag – het Engeland se magte, wat in die minderheid was, naby Azincourt (tans Frans spelling) triomfeer. Die Agincourt-alliansie, ondersteun deur historici en toerismegroepe, beoog om 'n 'Groot Skiet' aan te bied met rubber-stomp pylpyle met houtskagte en wit vere. Elke deelnemer sal 30 pyle skiet om die historiese salvo te herskep. Historici hoop hierdie gebeurtenis sal nuwe lig werp op debatte oor die langboog se deurslaggewende rol. Hedendaagse skattings dui op 12,000-36,000 Franse soldate wat teen 6,000-9,000 Engelse geveg het, met laasgenoemde se langboë (effektief tot 230 meter) as deurslaggewend. Die modderige, hellende terrein het Franse ridders se mobiliteit belemmer, met ongeveer 6,000 Franse slagoffers teenoor 400 Engelse. Terwyl Shakespeare die oorwinning verewig het, bevraagteken sommige geleerdes of taktiese voordele eerder as net boogskiet die oorwinning verseker het. Die herdenkingsgeleentheid sal op die bewaarde slagveld plaasvind, saam met ander Europese oorlogherdenkings. Streng veiligheidsreëls sal die nabaasting beheer, met 'n verbod op gevaarlike wapens.

article_content: Prosecutor Robert Colover has resigned from the Crown Prosecution Service's Rape Panel after an official review condemned his description of a 13-year-old abuse survivor as 'predatory.' The CPS announced Colover will no longer prosecute sexual offense cases following his inappropriate characterization of the minor during paedophile Neil Wilson's sentencing. At last month's Snaresbrook Crown Court hearing, Colover claimed the teenager had 'initiated sexual contact' with 41-year-old Wilson, describing her as 'experienced' and suggesting the offender had been 'coerced.' Child protection groups strongly criticized these remarks, warning such victim-blaming rhetoric could deter abuse survivors from coming forward. CPS Director Keir Starmer QC confirmed the language violated professional standards, stating Colover expressed regret for his word choice. The resignation forms part of broader CPS efforts to improve sensitivity in handling abuse cases.

Die KVD het bekend gemaak Colover sal nie meer seksuele misdryfsake hanteer nie ná sy onvanlike uitlatings oor die minderjarige tydens pedofiel Neil Wilson se vonnisoplegging. Tydens die verhoor by Snaresbrook Kroonhof verlede maand het Colover beweer die tiener het 'self seksuele kontak begin' met die 41-jarige oortreder, haar as 'seksueel ervare' beskryf en gesuggereer Wilson was 'onder druk geplaas.' Kinderveiligingsorganisasies het hierdie kommentare streng gekritiseer en gewaarsku sulke slagoffer-blamerende retoriek kan oorlewendes ontmoedig om hul gevalle aan te meld. KVD-direkteur Keir Starmer QC het bevestig die uitdrukkings het professionele standaarde oortree, met Colover wat openlike spyt uitgespreek het oor sy taalgebruik. Hierdie stap vorm deel van die KVD se breër inisiatief om hantering van misbruiksake met meer sensitiwiteit te benader.

article_content: Brianie Copeland, a 17-year-old from Bearpark, County Durham, faces significant challenges in pursuing her childcare career due to severe allergic reactions triggered by dust, eggs, pets, and synthetic fabrics. Despite managing her condition since childhood with her mother Pamela Donnelly's support, recent health deterioration during the holiday season has jeopardized her childcare qualification program at New College Durham. Brianie, who requires constant medication and avoids common products like makeup and hair treatments, fell behind in her nursery work placement due to illness-related absences. Her mother emphasizes the need for institutional support, stating: 'She has extra needs compared to other students that should be addressed.' College officials were unavailable for comment.

article_content: Southampton FC continues to impress in the Premier League despite losing five key players during the summer transfer window. Club legend Matt Le Tissier asserts the team now shows 'greater depth' under manager Ronald Koeman, with new signings making significant contributions. The Saints hold second place with 10 points from five matches. Despite £92.5 million in player sales to top clubs, Southampton's strategic recruitment includes striker Graziano Pelle (£9m from Feyenoord) with three goals, and creative midfielder Dusan Tadic (£10.9m from FC Twente) providing two assists. Defensive reinforcements Toby Alderweireld (loan) and Ryan Bertrand (loan) have strengthened the backline. Le Tissier noted: 'Koeman's done excellent work rebuilding the squad. We might actually be stronger than last season.' While acknowledging favorable early fixtures, he highlighted Pelle's adaptation and the potential of recent signings yet to feature regularly.

article_content: Bloomberg's £11,500 annual subscription service provides financial professionals with exclusive access to a luxury marketplace via fingerprint authentication. The platform features premium listings including a £10m Miami estate, rare timepieces like a £42,000 Patek Philippe, and high-end rentals such as a Hamptons property at £5,000 for three nights. Expanding beyond financial data, Bloomberg's 'Posh' section organizes listings into six categories: Travel, Cars, Property, Boats, Services, and Merchandise. While targeting affluent users, some accessible options appear, including £100 Mercedes accessories and a £10 store credit resale. Global offerings range from a £15.8m Italian castle to a £27,500 Dutch dressage horse. Upcoming 'Hotel' reviews will join existing restaurant (Dine) and flight (Fly) services in 2024, completing the luxury lifestyle ecosystem.

article_content: Iran has reached a historic agreement with the United States and five other world powers, implementing a temporary freeze on its nuclear program. This marks the most significant diplomatic breakthrough between Washington and Tehran in over three decades. President Hassan Rouhani confirmed the six-month agreement, which restricts Iran's nuclear activities in exchange for gradual sanctions relief, including access to £2.5 billion from oil revenues. The interim period allows further negotiations for a comprehensive long-term solution. U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry arrived at Stansted Airport after finalizing the deal in Geneva with counterparts from Russia, China, France, Britain, and Germany. The agreement limits uranium enrichment to 5% concentration - below weapons-grade levels - while permitting monitored civilian nuclear development. EU foreign policy chief Catherine Ashton and UK Foreign Secretary William Hague participated in the negotiations. President Obama praised the agreement's safeguards against nuclear weapon development: 'These measures block Iran's primary pathways to nuclear weapons.' However, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the deal as a 'historic mistake,' asserting Israel's right to self-defense. The White House emphasized ongoing monitoring provisions and the maintained framework of key economic sanctions.

article_content: A young legal professional tragically lost his life after wandering onto active railway tracks following an evening of heavy drinking, a London inquest revealed. Victor Carles Quiros, 24, consumed four bottles of wine and shared half a bottle of whisky with three companions during a social gathering at his cousin's Kensington apartment before the fatal April 12 incident. Security footage showed Quiros entering Ladbroke Grove Underground Station's restricted area around 5:25 AM while visibly intoxicated. The Panama-born lawyer walked along the Hammersmith & City line tracks before being struck by a train traveling at 40mph. Postmortem reports confirmed a blood alcohol concentration of 200-300mg per 100ml - triple the UK's legal driving limit and at levels medical experts associate with potential coma induction. Train operator Jason Archer recounted the unavoidable collision: 'He appeared suddenly on the tracks without reacting to the approaching train. There was no time to prevent impact.' Quiros' cousin Orlando Vasquesz noted the deceased had left his wallet, keys, and coat behind, indicating severe alcohol-induced disorientation. Coroner Dr. William Dolman officially ruled the death accidental, confirming Quiros' extreme intoxication impaired his decision-making. Colleagues at international law firm Arias, Fabrega and Fabrega memorialized Quiros as 'an extraordinary professional and human being' in their heartfelt public tribute.

article_content: The ATP World Tour Finals have become a financial pillar for men's tennis since relocating to London in 2009, drawing massive crowds and elevating players' star status. As this year's event highlights the tournament's value to host cities, questions arise about whether London will retain it beyond 2015 or if it will resume its previous nomadic pattern. New York and Rio de Janeiro were previously considered as alternatives. While New York boasts tennis heritage from its 1977-1989 hosting era and current US Open infrastructure, Rio represents an emerging market preparing for the 2016 Olympics. However, ATP officials caution that relocation carries financial risks. Tournament director Andre Silva notes extending London's tenure remains 'definitely possible,' emphasizing stability over experimentation. Roger Federer (who recently tied Ivan Lendl's record of 12 Finals appearances) supports this view, stating venues need time to establish roots rather than short-term 'circus' stops. Financial data reinforces London's appeal: The O2 Arena partnership generates consistent revenue through 17,800-seat capacity and dual daily sessions. Over one million attendees have visited since the 2009 debut, with ticket prices ranging from £10-£105. Critics note challenges in other regions: Shanghai faced time zone issues affecting European viewers and lower early-round attendance, while UK tax laws occasionally draw player complaints. Despite this, stakeholders like retired ATP executive Richard Davies credit London with doubling previous host cities' financial returns through corporate partnerships and reliable fan engagement.

article_content: ISLAMABAD, Pakistan (CNN) – Hours after declaring a state of emergency Saturday, Pakistani President Pervez Musharraf deployed troops to seize broadcasting equipment from a television station and placed a prominent opposition leader under house arrest. In a televised address, Musharraf justified his actions as necessary for national stability while suspending the constitution and dismissing Supreme Court Chief Justice Iftikhar Mohammed Chaudhry for the second time. On Sunday, police arrested Javed Hashmi, acting president of ex-Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's opposition party, along with 10 aides. Hashmi was detained upon leaving his residence in Multan. Musharraf described Pakistan as facing 'a critical and dangerous juncture' due to escalating tensions and terrorism during his national address. The Supreme Court immediately challenged the emergency declaration as unlawful, asserting Musharraf lacked authority to suspend the constitution. Security forces subsequently removed Chaudhry from office, replacing him with Justice Abdul Hameed Dogar via state television announcement. Media outlets faced severe restrictions, with AAJ-TV's Islamabad office raided by police who confiscated equipment. New regulations threaten three-year prison sentences and $70,000 fines for criticizing government leaders, according to AAJ news director Talat Hussain. U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice condemned the measures during an Iraq conference in Turkey, stating: 'Anything that takes Pakistan off the democratic path is highly regrettable.' Pakistani officials claimed the emergency would be temporary, with Ambassador Mahmud Ali Durrani assuring democratic progress would resume. Musharraf's contested October re-election remains pending Supreme Court validation amid eligibility challenges. The president maintains he will relinquish military command before his new term begins November 15 and promises parliamentary elections by January 15. Opposition leader Imran Khan reported house arrest in Lahore, vowing resistance against Musharraf's 'emergency drama.' Former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, recently returned from exile, criticized the crackdown as she campaigns for her Pakistan People's Party ahead of scheduled elections.

article_content: The United Nations projects global population will surpass seven billion within days, continuing a rapid growth trajectory that saw numbers triple since 1940. Current estimates predict eight billion by 2025 and ten billion before the end of the 21st century, with the Asia-Pacific region expected to account for the majority of near-term growth. This expansion raises significant concerns about resource allocation, particularly food production and healthcare infrastructure. Developing nations face disproportionate challenges, with sub-Saharan Africa projected to add over one billion residents and South Asia 630 million by 2050. Experts warn this growth could exacerbate existing inequalities, as poorer populations dependent on natural resources struggle against wealthier competitors. Simultaneously, aging populations in industrialized nations strain pension and healthcare systems, exemplified by Japan's 20-year doubling of citizens aged 65+. UN officials acknowledge improved survival rates, noting a child born today has better five-year survival prospects than a decade ago. However, they emphasize the urgent need for sustainable policies addressing contraception access, agricultural innovation, and economic reforms. Harvard's Professor David Bloom warns against complacency, stating: 'We must address demographic challenges proactively through improved family planning, child survival initiatives, and revised immigration policies.' While global population growth has slowed from its 1968 peak of 2% to 1.1% annually, the addition of 78 million people this year underscores ongoing pressures. The UK's own growth pattern mirrors global trends, expanding from 10.5 million in 1801 to 62.5 million today.

Terselfdertyd belas verouderende bevolkings in geïndustrialiseerde lande pensioen- en gesondheidsorgstelsels, soos blyk uit Japan se verdubbeling van inwoners ouer as 65 oor 20 jaar. article_content: A Massachusetts municipal worker faces career consequences after an unconventional animal rescue operation. Jim Mackie, former Highway Superintendent for Phillipston, lost his position following his use of town equipment to retrieve his partner's stranded feline in neighboring Westminster. The May incident occurred when Jackie Prime's cat Kaboodle became trapped in a tall tree during stormy weather. After failed attempts to secure help from local fire services and arborists, Mackie utilized a Phillipston bucket truck for the rescue. Complications arose when the vehicle became mired in soft ground, requiring additional municipal machinery for extraction. Town officials investigated the off-jurisdiction equipment usage, resulting in Mackie's two-week unpaid suspension and eventual termination when the Board of Selectmen chose not to renew his position. article_content: (CNN) -- High-frequency trading (HFT) uses advanced algorithms and ultra-fast computers to execute millions of trades daily across global markets. While proponents argue HFT reduces volatility and lowers costs for small investors, critics highlight risks like the May 6, 2010 'Flash Crash' that temporarily erased nearly 1,000 points from the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The relentless pursuit of speed has sparked a technological arms race featuring dedicated trading circuits, optimized fiber routes through mountains, straighter transatlantic cables, and microwave networks exploiting faster air-based signal transmission. Evolutionary 'genetic' trading algorithms now adapt in real-time, while even long-term pension funds engage in HFT strategies. Einstein's universal speed limit - light travels one foot per nanosecond in vacuum - leaves room for infrastructure improvements. Faster firms dominate slower competitors, mirroring ecological predator-prey dynamics. Emerging micro-duration options markets aim to hedge HFT risks. Two critical issues emerge: 1) No scientific framework exists to predict failures in light-speed financial networks 2) Regulators lack tools to manage this complexity. Researchers identified 'sub-second tsunamis' - instant price crashes undetectable by humans - that preceded the 2008 crisis, particularly in banks later associated with the financial meltdown. The solution requires a collaborative 'financial Manhattan Project' combining real-time market modeling, complex systems theory, and algorithm monitoring while preserving trade secrets. article_content: Taylor Anderson's journey to Japan fulfilled a childhood dream that began with middle school language studies. The 24-year-old from Virginia had spent over two years teaching English to elementary and middle school students in Ishinomaki when disaster struck with the March 11, 2011 earthquake and subsequent tsunami. Friends recall her tireless efforts to share Japanese culture - from organizing literature events to surprising sorority sisters with traditional snacks. 'She made us all feel connected to her passion,' said friend Katie Garin Langley. Her final confirmed act mirrored her caring nature: ensuring students' safety before attempting to bike home through the disaster zone. The Randolph-Macon graduate's disappearance sparked international attention until Monday's heartbreaking confirmation from U.S. officials. College president Robert Lindgren noted: 'Her story teaches us about pursuing purpose.' Former classmates describe an irrepressible spirit whose kindness continues inspiring others. 'Taylor's light lives through everyone she touched,' reflected friend Virginia Seatherton.

article_content: (CNN) -- A virulent E. coli strain has caused 19 deaths and over 2,000 infections across 12 European countries, the World Health Organization (WHO) reported Saturday. Germany accounts for 18 fatalities, with officials stating it remains too early to confirm if the outbreak has peaked. Sweden reported one death. Germany has recorded 573 cases of hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) - a severe kidney failure condition - marking the highest global HUS count in any recorded outbreak. WHO confirms 12 German deaths from HUS and six from enterohemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC), a strain causing intestinal hemorrhaging with symptoms including abdominal cramps and bloody diarrhea. Approximately 1,428 patients have the EHEC strain without HUS progression. Other affected nations include Austria, Czech Republic, Denmark, France, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Spain, Switzerland, and the UK. While initial reports linked the outbreak to Spanish organic cucumbers distributed via Germany, contamination sources remain unconfirmed. Germany's Robert Koch Institute advises against consuming raw tomatoes, cucumbers, and lettuce. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration's David Elder stated all German and Spanish vegetable imports will undergo testing before sale, representing a small fraction of U.S. produce supplies. Three Americans visiting northern Germany remain hospitalized with HUS, while two U.S. service members in Germany experienced non-critical symptoms. CDC's Chris Braden emphasized no expected U.S. spread.

Duitsland verteenwoordig 18 sterftes, met amptenare wat sê dit is steeds te vroeg om te bevestig of die uitbraak sy hoogtepunt bereik het. Swede het een doodgeval aangemeld. Duitsland het 573 gevalle van hemolitiese uremiese sindroom (HUS) aangeteken - 'n ernstige nierfalingstoestand - wat die hoogste geregistreerde HUS-syfers wêreldwyd aandui. Die WGO bevestig 12 Duitse sterftes aan HUS en ses aan enterohemorragiese E. coli (EHEC), 'n stam wat dermbloedinge veroorsaak met simptome soos buikkrampe en bloedige diarree. Ongeveer 1 428 pasiënte het die EHEC-stam sonder HUS-ontwikkeling. Ander geraakte lande sluit Oostenryk, Tsjeggië, Denemarke, Frankryk, Nederland, Noorweë, Pole, Spanje, Switserland en die Verenigde Koninkryk in. Hoewel aanvanklike berigte die uitbraak aan Spaanse organiese komkommers versprei via Duitsland gekoppel het, bly besmettingsbronne onbevestig. Duitsland se Robert Koch-instituut raai aan om nie rou tamaties, komkommers en blaarsla te eet nie. article_content: Bodybuilder Blake Beckford has defied medical expectations by becoming a fitness model after undergoing life-changing surgery for ulcerative colitis. The 33-year-old from Stratford-upon-Avon had his colon removed in a sub-total colectomy at Oxford's John Radcliffe Hospital and now uses a colostomy bag, following a decade-long battle with the inflammatory bowel condition that required up to 20 daily bathroom visits and caused a 2-stone weight loss. Despite doctors warning that intensive training would be 'very unattainable' due to risks of hernias, Beckford began a rigorous regime in January 2023. He has since gained 1 stone 4 pounds (13st 2lbs) in muscle mass and secured a feature in Men's Fitness magazine. Now working as a personal trainer, Beckford aims to compete in the physique category of October's Miami Pro UK Championships while advocating for stoma awareness. 'I want to show society that having a stoma doesn't define you,' Beckford stated. 'You can be attractive, achieve goals, and live fully.' His journey included overcoming initial self-consciousness about the visible medical device, eventually embracing it as part of his identity after undergoing an ileostomy procedure that diverted his small intestine through an abdominal opening.

article_content: LOS ANGELES (CNN) – While Katherine Jackson observes religious traditions that preclude birthday or Mother's Day festivities, the matriarch of the Jackson family acknowledges the emotional power of floral gestures. As she approaches her 81st birthday on May 4, the mother of late pop icon Michael Jackson revealed her collaboration with SendHerFlowers.com for this Tuesday's debut of the Katherine Jackson Flower Collection. 'Flowers symbolize affection – a tangible way to say 'You're in my thoughts,'' Jackson shared. 'They lift spirits during difficult moments.' The interview marked a rare public appearance for Jackson, who avoided detailed discussion about ongoing legal matters surrounding her son's estate or the impending trial of Dr. Conrad Murray, charged in Michael Jackson's 2009 death. Though visibly uneasy about the two-month court proceedings scheduled to begin May 9 – which may include graphic autopsy photos – Jackson confirmed her attendance. 'A mother's responsibilities never cease,' she stated. Off-camera, Jackson expressed frustration with media portrayals of her marriage, clarifying that despite living separately from husband Joe Jackson in Las Vegas, they maintain regular contact and public solidarity. Having recently relocated from the family's longtime Encino estate to a Calabasas hilltop property, Jackson emphasized maternal dedication while raising Michael's three children. 'Mothers must remain present and consistent – your word becomes their compass,' advised the woman who raised nine children. 'We're the adhesive binding families together.'

article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) -- Smartphones may help retailers better understand purchasing patterns and deliver real-time discounts to shoppers. Gary Schwartz, CEO of mobile technology firm Impact Mobile, stated that mobile marketing will become crucial for retailers within two years. He noted that nearly half of current mobile devices are smartphones, with projections suggesting 70% adoption within two years. Consumers can opt-in to receive alerts and promotions from retailers, enabling businesses to track shopping behaviors. Schwartz emphasized that strategic smartphone use could boost sales and stimulate economic growth. 'When implemented wisely, it will significantly increase sales,' he added. The Gap and its subsidiaries Old Navy and Banana Republic have partnered with Visa on the 'Gap Mobile4U' app. 'We send shoppers relevant offers based on their location near stores or within malls,' explained Amy Carr, Gap's senior director of customer relationship marketing. The technology tracks customer proximity to physical locations to deliver targeted promotions. Digital marketing consultant Zachary Cohen describes this location-based marketing as the 'Wild West,' citing unclear regulations. 'Current laws lack clarity because legislators struggle to understand the technology,' Cohen noted. He expressed concerns about potential smartphone spam invading personal devices. Carr maintains that retailers self-regulate to avoid customer dissatisfaction from excessive messaging. 'It's too risky to annoy potential customers with unwanted alerts that drain battery life or data,' she said. Participation remains optional for consumers. While some shoppers like Los Angeles resident David Thomason criticize the technology as invasive, others have embraced it. Carr reported high participation rates but declined to share specific sales data. The company uses unique promotional codes to measure the program's effectiveness as the technology continues developing.

'Ons stuur klante relevante aanbiedinge gebaseer op hul ligging naby winkels of in winkelsentrums,' het Amy Carr, Gap se senior direkteur van kliënteverhoudingsbemarking, verduidelik. Regarding tragedies like the 2014 Peshawar school massacre, Welby cautioned against blaming religion exclusively, noting its use as 'a simple hook for complex problems.' article_content: A Malaysian appellate court reversed opposition leader Anwar Ibrahim's 2012 acquittal on sodomy charges Friday, renewing debates about judicial independence. Previous convictions led to six years' imprisonment until partial exoneration in 2004. Remaining legal restrictions prevented him from holding office until 2008, the year his coalition secured 82 parliamentary seats - unprecedented opposition gains.

article_content: Rosalia Mera, the Spanish business magnate who co-created global fashion giant Zara, passed away at 69 following a stroke during her stay on Menorca. The Galicia-born entrepreneur was transferred to her hometown hospital in La Coruna where she died on August 15, 2013. Starting as an 11-year-old school dropout working as a seamstress, Mera revolutionized retail by establishing Zara in 1975 with former spouse Armancio Ortega. Their brand's strategy of delivering designer-inspired looks at accessible prices propelled Inditex SA - Zara's parent company - to operate 1,763 stores worldwide as documented in 2013 records. The company's popularity surged through high-profile admirers like the Duchess of Cambridge, who wore a Zara dress post-wedding, and Kim Sears, spotted in their designs during Wimbledon 2013. Holding 5.1% of Inditex shares, Mera ranked as the world's wealthiest self-made woman according to Forbes' 2013 list, with a £3.9bn fortune. Beyond business, she actively opposed Spain's proposed abortion restrictions and education/healthcare budget cuts. Inditex's official statement mourned 'a fundamental figure in the company's creation and growth', extending condolences to her family and friends.

Die eenheid het in samewerking met ander agentskappe verskeie eiendomme ondersoek. Baie hiervan behoort aan Zandile Gumede, voormalige eThekwini-burgemeester.  ’n Lasbrief is by Gumede se huis in Inanda afgelewer. Valke-woordvoerder Hangwani Mulaudzi het gesê Gumede moet aandui waar addisionele bates is. “Nadat dit voltooi is, sal die meeste items gestoor word. Sy het die reg om die hof te nader as sy die optrede wil betwis,” het hy gesê.  Gumede se regspan was teenwoordig tydens die lasbrieflevering. Die Valke het eers na haar Umhlanga-huis gegaan, maar het ontdek dat dit sedert Julie verhuur word – ’n oortreding van haar borgtogvoorwaardes wat die huis as permanente woning aandui.  Mulaudzi het gesê hierdie kwessie geniet prioriteit.  Meer as R50 miljoen se bates is tot dusver beslag gelê, insluitend eiendomme in Zimbali en Umhlanga Rocks, luukse voertuie, bates in trusts en maatskappye, asook kontant in bankrekeninge, volgens NVG-woordvoerder Natasha Kara.  Gumede verskyn saam met raadslid Mondli Mthembu en sakeman Craig Poonan in die Durbanse handelshof oor ’n R200 miljoen vasteafvalkontrak uit 2016. Almal is op R50 000 borg vrygelaat.  Hulle word aangekla van bedrog, oortreding van die Wet op Munisipale Finansiële Bestuur, asook oortredings van die Wet op Georganiseerde Misdaad. Gumede en Mthembu word ook aangekla vir die aanhitsing van ’n onwettige byeenkoms teen stadsbestuurder Sipho Nzuza in April.  Die ANC het Gumede in Augustus herontplooi ná haar aanvanklike weiering om haar amp as burgemeester te verlaat.

Die verdagtes verskyn die week in die Orkney-landdroshof op aanklagte van moord, poging tot moord, roof en besit van gesteelde goedere. Sers. article_content: 26 September 2013 deur Susan Lombaard  Besoekers strek hulle uit op sagte matrassies terwyl hulle na die vertoning op die plafon staar  Die produksie Tussen hemel en aarde bied 'n unieke teaterervaring waar matrassies tradisionele sitplekke vervang. Soos TT Cloete se digkuns die gewone omverwerp, so daag hierdie opvoering jou persepsie van verhoogkuns uit.  Pieter Lombaard en Alexa Strachan se konsep kombineer Cloete se verwonderende verse oor die skepping - van mierekolonies tot sterrestelsels - met Herman van den Berg se musiek en dinamiese plafonprojeksies. Terwyl jy op jou rug lê, sweef die beelde bokant jou en meng dit met Chris van Niekerk se voordrag en fragmente van 'n onderhoud met Cloete.  Die kamera-hoeke skep soms 'n virtuele wereld wat jou insluit - 'n soort driedimensionele ervaring sonder brille. Selfs met toe oë bly die digterlike reis voortduur deur die krag van klank en taal.  'Ons het verse gekies wat 'n skeppingsverhaal vertel,' verduidelik Lombaard. Dis nie net 'n opvoering nie, maar 'n ervaring wat jou liggaam laat rus terwyl jou verstand reis.  Aardklop-kuiergers: Moet hierdie 35-minute wonder miskien nie! Vir R60 kry jy nie net digkuns nie, maar 'n kans om weer soos 'n kind na die wêreld te kyk. Theo de Jager (AgriSA) se 2012-voorspelling van 10 000 ton mielies het nie verwesenlik nie – hulle het net 2 400 ton geoes.
